tasks.label: Build Maize v2 (mzvm) and run its fixtures
tasks.detail: maize-418: build the v2 machine (mzvm, mzvmg) and its fixture binary, then run the v2 fixtures only. This is the fast v2 loop and it is what Ctrl+Shift+B runs. It assumes the preset's build directory is already configured; if it is not, run one of the install or build-world tasks once first. The v2 machine has no assembler and no device surface yet, so mzvm's output is the register dump from --registers rather than anything a program prints.

windows.command: cmake --build build/windows-llvm-mingw-debug --target mzvm mzvmg mzvm_v2_fixtures && ctest --test-dir build/windows-llvm-mingw-debug -L v2 --output-on-failure

linux.command: cmake --build build/linux-debug --target mzvm mzvmg mzvm_v2_fixtures && ctest --test-dir build/linux-debug -L v2 --output-on-failure

osx.command: cmake --build build/macos-debug --target mzvm mzvmg mzvm_v2_fixtures && ctest --test-dir build/macos-debug -L v2 --output-on-failure

tasks.label: Assemble current .mazm
tasks.detail: Run mazm on the active file; errors land in the Problems panel and are click-to-navigate.

tasks.label: Check current .mazm (no output file)
tasks.detail: mazm --check on the active file: same clickable errors, zero filesystem effects (no .mzb written, stale .mzb kept).

tasks.label: Build everything (build-world)
tasks.detail: Build the native binaries + tools, the C cross toolchain, quesOS, the wave-1 userland, and the demos, all in one call. Slower than the binaries-only install task below; run it after a fresh clone or pull. On Windows this runs natively via Git Bash, no WSL involved.

tasks.label: Install maize + maizeg + mzvm + mzvmg + mazm + mzld + mzdis to ~/bin
tasks.detail: Build maize (console) + maizeg (graphical/SDL), the Maize v2 machine mzvm + mzvmg, and mazm, mzld, and mzdis, and copy them to the user bin directory so editors find stable copies on PATH, then refresh the C cross-toolchain (cproc/qbe + Maize target) so mzcc stays current. Fast binaries-only loop; use Build everything (build-world) for the full "I pulled" rebuild. On Windows this runs natively via Git Bash, no WSL involved.
